coordinate_policy: The coordinate pairs copied from individual NIAH pages are page-displayed values whose CRS is not explicitly labelled on those pages. Their magnitudes are consistent with the older Irish Grid/National Grid representation, not ITM EPSG:2157. The official NIAH national dataset publishes distinct ITM_E/ITM_N, latitude/longitude and National Grid coordinate fields. Keep page-displayed pairs as raw source evidence only; do not label them ITM, convert them, or import them into national_grid_reference, latitude/longitude or map_url until matched to the correctly identified official coordinate fields and an approved CRS-aware policy.

object_records.name: 146 Parnell Street, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
object_records.historical_description: Terraced two-bay four-storey house built c.1770, now recorded as a hostel. It has a pitched slate roof behind a rebuilt parapet with squared granite coping; English garden-wall-bond red brick walls; gauged flat-arched window openings with brick reveals and granite sills; and nineteenth-century replacement timber sliding sash windows. The round-headed entrance is set within a tooled sandstone doorcase with channelled pilasters, scrolled brackets and an open-bed pediment.
object_records.historical_significance: NIAH describes the house as pleasantly proportioned and probably among the earliest surviving buildings in the vicinity. Its mid- to late-eighteenth-century sandstone doorcase and historic timber sash windows are key features; the English garden-wall bond is a notable material distinction.
object_records.access_status: Hostel/commercial premises. Photograph the exterior from the public footpath only; interior access requires permission.
object_records.photography_restrictions: No access permission is implied. Respect residents, staff, occupiers and visitors. Do not enter private or restricted areas; obtain permission for interior or commercial photography.

object_records.name: 156 Parnell Street, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
object_records.historical_description: Terraced two-bay four-storey former house, built c.1800. The NIAH record describes handmade red brick in Flemish bond, raised brick quoins, a hipped slate roof, and a replacement timber shopfront. Upper openings include uPVC casements. The survey record described the property as vacant at the time of survey; that is historical survey information, not a statement about present occupancy.
object_records.historical_significance: NIAH identifies the building as an early nineteenth-century Georgian townhouse contributing to the varied historic terrace on Parnell Street. Its balanced proportions and plain architectural treatment retain streetscape value despite later alterations.
object_records.access_status: Commercial premises or property with occupancy to be checked. Photograph only from lawful public space; do not infer current vacancy from the historic NIAH survey.

object_records.name: 103–104 Parnell Street, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
object_records.historical_description: One combined NIAH record for a terraced four-bay two-storey former pair of houses over a concealed basement. No. 103 retains a c.1900 timber shopfront with fluted Ionic pilasters and a figurative lion in the pediment; No. 104 has a more recent shopfront. The combined registration represents one surveyed property record, not two independent NIAH objects.
object_records.historical_significance: NIAH notes the unusual massing and later unification as evidence of the property's architectural development. The appraisal records a long association with grocery and spirit dealing and later use as the Blue Lion bar.
object_records.access_status: Commercial frontage. Photograph from the public footpath only; do not enter premises or photograph staff/customers without permission.
object_records.photography_restrictions: No access permission is implied. Respect residents, staff, occupiers and visitors. Do not enter private or restricted areas; obtain permission for interior or commercial photography.

object_records.name: 98 Parnell Street, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
object_records.historical_description: Terraced two-bay four-storey former townhouse with a four-storey rear return. The NIAH record describes Flemish-bond red brick, segmental-headed openings with gauged brick voussoirs and stop-chamfered reveals, timber sash windows, and a c.1900 timber shopfront with fluted pilasters, pedimented brackets and cornice.
object_records.historical_significance: NIAH highlights the unusual stop-chamfered window reveals and the building's role as a local social hub. The record documents the Healy family grocery association from at least the mid-nineteenth century to c.1950.
object_records.access_status: Commercial/public-house history. Photograph the exterior from the public footpath only; no interior access is implied.
object_records.photography_restrictions: No access permission is implied. Respect residents, staff, occupiers and visitors. Do not enter private or restricted areas; obtain permission for interior or commercial photography.

object_records.name: Desmonds / Not to Worry / Talbot Street Business Centre, 19 Talbot Street, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
object_records.historical_description: Terraced three-bay three-storey house recorded with a house/shop use history. The NIAH record describes Flemish-bond brown brick, a hipped slate roof, two-over-two timber sliding sash windows, and a three-centred-arch entrance with moulded surround, painted Ionic doorcase and granite entrance step.
object_records.historical_significance: NIAH notes that, despite later shopfront alterations, the building retains its original form and fabric, including the Ionic doorcase and sash windows. It contributes to the historic terrace rhythm on the north side of Talbot Street.
object_records.access_status: Business premises. Photograph the exterior from the public footpath only; interior access requires permission.
object_records.photography_restrictions: No access permission is implied. Respect residents, staff, occupiers and visitors. Do not enter private or restricted areas; obtain permission for interior or commercial photography.
